telc A1 Exam: Format, Pass Mark and Preparation

Prepare for Start Deutsch 1 / telc Deutsch A1 with timings, scoring guidance, official mock material, speaking practice and a focused study checklist.

Start Deutsch 1 / telc Deutsch A1 · Source checked 14 November 2026

See the exam formatOfficial mock and sources

Choose the correct examination

This page covers the general adult Start Deutsch 1 / telc Deutsch A1 examination. A1 Junior and A1 for migrants are different named products. Begin by matching the full exam name to your booking and to the organisation requesting proof.

Exam format and timing

Published task times; arrival, breaks and appointment length are separate.
PartTask timeWhat to check
ListeningAbout 20 minutesThree parts; work with the audio instructions rather than assuming every recording is repeated.
Reading and writing45 minutes combinedThree reading parts and two writing parts share this block.
SpeakingAbout 15 minutesThree parts, usually with four candidates and no preparation time.

These are the published standard task times, not a promise of total appointment length. Follow the centre’s instructions for your booked format, breaks and any approved accommodations.

Scoring and partial examinations

The official linked mock assigns 60 points in total: 15 each for listening, reading, writing and speaking. Its pass band starts at 36 points. Do not apply Goethe’s 100-point scale to this telc practice result.

The product page says this exam cannot be taken as a partial examination. Plan for the whole test and confirm any new booking with the centre.

Switching from Goethe A1?

Goethe A1 and telc A1 share a beginner CEFR target and similar everyday functions, but use provider-specific marking and materials. A Goethe score prediction is not a telc score conversion.

Read the Goethe A1 guide before transferring a study plan between providers.

Prepare each skill

Listening

Practise names, numbers, times and short messages. After an error, replay the relevant sentence and identify the word that changes the answer. A familiar noun alone may be a distractor.

Reading

Use notices, brief emails and everyday information. Distinguish what a text explicitly says from what sounds plausible. Copy names and dates carefully when the task requires a form.

Writing

Practise filling a form and writing a short response to the supplied situation. Cover each requested detail before adding extra sentences; check the greeting, verb and closing against the recipient.

Speaking

Prepare a flexible introduction, simple information questions and requests. Work with a partner who changes the object or topic so you must listen and respond instead of reciting a fixed speech.

Build a preparation sequence

The following is Klarweg’s study advice, not an official schedule or a promise that a set number of weeks produces this level. Adjust the sequence after a diagnostic attempt.

  1. Diagnose. Try the official mock without a timer and list missing vocabulary separately from misunderstood task instructions.
  2. Build. Rotate number listening, form filling, short messages and spoken requests. Repeat a weak function in a different context.
  3. Rehearse. Use the written time blocks and practise a small-group speaking exchange. Review with the official key and writing/speaking criteria.

Mistakes to avoid

  • Learning only a self-introduction while neglecting questions and requests.
  • Spending too much of the combined reading/writing block on one difficult item.
  • Treating another provider’s A1 result or a memorised text as proof of readiness.

Check readiness before booking

  • I can identify the exact adult A1 test on my booking.
  • I can complete a simple form legibly and check spelling.
  • I can ask and answer short questions without a script.
  • I have checked the centre’s ID, arrival and speaking-session instructions.

Use the official answer key for objective items. For writing and speaking, compare the published criteria and seek specific feedback; an unchecked self-score is not a reliable pass prediction.

Common questions

Is telc A1 the same as Goethe A1?

They target the same CEFR level, but are separate examinations. Match the required certificate and use the booked provider’s material.

Can I book just speaking?

The official telc A1 product page does not offer this as a partial examination. Ask the centre about a complete booking.

Fees, dates and your exam centre

Ask the examination centre for the current fee, available date, full examination name, delivery format, cancellation terms and identification rules. This guide does not sell places, guarantee availability or quote a nationwide fee.

Find an examination centre through telc and confirm that it offers your exact test. If a certificate is needed for admission, work or an official process, confirm acceptance with the receiving organisation.
